sections.html: Among the smallest species of tetra is Hyphessobrycon elachys, the veilfin tetra from Paraguay. The species becomes only 1.5-2 cm long (standard length without caudal fin).

It is almost impossible to tell H. elachys from these other tetras apart on basis of the coloration. So imports of the species are always a mix, sometimes H. elachys is hardly represented in them at all. So to a certain degree there are always bycatches among H. elachys, but the current import contains at least 90% veilfin tetras.
The charming animals inhabit swampy areas in the Rio Paraguay drainage.
In the natural habitat Hyphessobrycon elachys lives in mixed schools along with other, very similar tetras and Corydoras hastatus.
The veilfin tetra is unique by the shape of the anal fin in males, the very long ventral fins in males and teeth structures.

The genus Hyphessobrycon, as it is currently defined, represents an artificial assemblage of species which are not very closely related. So the placement of H. elachys in Hyphessobrycon is only provisional and it will surely be placed in another genus in case of a revision of Hyphessobrycon.
